recipes.name: Venison Tequila Chili
ingredients_raw: 2 (15 ounce) cans chili beans in sauce

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the ground venison and cook, stirring to crumble, until no longer pink. Mix in the celery and onion; cook and stir until tender. Season with red pepper flakes, garlic powder and chili powder. Cook and stir for a minute to intensify the flavors.
Pour in the tomatoes, tomato sauce, tequila and orange juice; simmer over low heat, uncovered, for 2 hours. After 2 hours, mix the beans into the chili and simmer for another 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Venison Tequila Chili
raw_recipe.description: A hearty venison chili made with tomatoes, onion and beans. Tequila gives it a boost of flavor. Adjust the spices to your taste.

review.reviewBody:
The is a FANTASTIC venison chili recipe!! I made some changes, but LOVED how it turned out. Used one white onion, 3 stalks of celery, a fresh serrano pepper minced (with seeds left in tact), a green pepper, added dried: cilantro, thyme, oregano, paprika, garlic granules, a dash of cinnamon, salt & pepper. I also used a small amount of agave syrup to mellow out the tomato acidity. Then I added 2 cans of diced tomatoes, a can of tomato paste & sauce & a can of chicken broth. For the beans I used 2 cans of great northern white beans, drained. I omitted the o.j., but we LOVED the addition of the tequila!! It's subtle, but you can taste it in the background -- yummy!!!

Thanks for posting this recipe :)

This recipe was very good. I pretty much followed it as written but did make the following changes:

1. I used fresh jalapeno instead of red pepper flakes and sauteed them with the onion & celery.

2. I added more chili powder, plus used cumin, coriander, and cayenne pepper.

3. I omitted the orange juice. Other reviewers have said that this lends a nice flavor but I don't think orange juice has any place in chili.

The end result was quite tasty. I didn't even need to add sour cream to my bowl (a chili staple). In fact, the sour cream ruined it for me which is testimony to how tasty this chili is on its own.
 
My only complaint is that it was too runny. Next time, I will pull back on the sauce or add more meat. Otherwise, this is definitely a keeper and I will make it again.
Great with a bag of dried kidney beans. Added 2 Tablespoons of Cocoa powder to deepen the flavors.
Just made this fantastic chili! Took suggestions from other reviewers and used ground beef and added 1 tablespoon brown sugar, and 2 tablespoons cocoa powder. Everything else the same.

We LOVED this chili! Had to make a few changes, subbed out black beans for chili beans and added about 1-2 cups beef stock since this was a long cook time, and need moisture added. I've had a ton of venison sausage in my time, but this is only me second time having ground venison and I must say, it beats the pants off ground beef in flavor lol! Loved it!!
Excellent...I added a half of a bottle of Newcastle beer to it, as well as the tequila. I believe next time, I'll add some beef broth...it was just a little thick as written.

Good. I made this in the crockpot. I browned the beef with the onions, then added that along with the remainder of the ingredients to the crockpot. Also, I omitted the OJ because we didn't have any. Next time, I will add some chopped green bell pepper. Served with Beer Bread I from this site.
Not a huge fan of venision but we had some given to us so I mixed it with beef and made this recipe. Great with some cayenne pepper and jalapenos!

Great recipe! I tweaked it a little bit by adding a couple of bell peppers, a can of corn, a tsp of cumin and a tsp of cayenne pepper. I also had some fresh parsley that needed to be used up, so I tossed some of that in as well. The tequila definitely adds some kick, and the OJ gives a bit of sweetness. Very good!
Excellent recipe. Didn't have any tequila, but it still turned out great. Added some brown sugar to cut back on the acidity, helps with heart burn. No leftovers. Will be making it again!!

Very hearty and delicious! I agree with the person who was worried about the 1/4 cup of chili powder but it worked very well. 

I added one jalapeno pepper and one serrano pepper for some heat but I could have added more as just those two only spiced it up a little bit.
This is the BEST chili!!!! Flavor is SO GOOD!! Definitely going to make again, made it exactly as written, only I added beans in last 30 minutes of the 2 hour simmer!! Thank you for sharing!!!
No Tequila
I made this recipe, according to the directions. I served it over corn chips, and topped it with shredded cheese. It was a little bland for my taste, so I added some hot sauce before serving it.
Fantastic recipe!

I tried this recipe because it was specific to venison and had good reviews. It did not disappoint! There was no gamey flavor, even when eating the leftovers. It needs a little more spiciness though, and what is chili without some peppers?! It needs peppers and Vegetables. So it will be 5 stars with some some simple adjustments.
I didn't add the tequila or orange juice but it was still delicious!!
I loved this recipe. I made a lot less than the recipe called for but no biggie...I changed a couple of ingredients but oh man this is the best I've ever had. I'm so glad I found this recipe
Taste was bland. Definitely needed something, but not sure what.
This is my go to chili recipe! Always a hit as is...
